title: Illbleed
subtitle: Six attractions and missing friends
summary: Illbleed is Crazy Games' survival horror adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 29 March 2001.
body: Illbleed is Crazy Games' survival horror adventure, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 29 March 2001. Eriko Christy enters a horror amusement park to find her missing friends, passing through six attractions based on fictional films. Each location supplies its own story and hazards, with a deliberately lurid sense of humour connecting the park. Producer Shinya Nishigaki's team had previously made Blue Stinger under the name Climax Graphics. Here, the main problem becomes recognising the next fright before it strikes, turning the conventions of a haunted attraction into a system to learn.

A sensory display reacts to sights, sounds, smells and a sixth sense as the character approaches an item or possible trap. The Horror Monitor lets the player mark suspicious places and investigate them, spending adrenaline in the process. Correctly identifying a trap disables it and returns the spent resource. Marking an enemy can also provide an opening advantage in combat. The player therefore reads the room through both its appearance and those sensory warnings, deciding which ordinary-looking object deserves attention before another step turns suspicion into damage.

Survival depends on stamina, heart rate and bleeding as well as the next enemy. Physical injury and sudden frights affect those measures differently, making the park dangerous in more than one way. Rescued friends become playable characters with their own strengths, while recovery items and upgrades can be purchased between expeditions. The system gives Illbleed's exaggerated horror a practical consequence: being frightened is something the character's body must withstand. Its dark comedy comes from learning to inspect an absurd spectacle carefully enough to survive the trick hidden inside it.
